report.tagline: A website where you describe an app in plain words and an AI agent builds, hosts and launches it for you.
report.simpleSummary: Replit lets anyone make a working app or website by chatting with an AI. You type something like 'build me a booking app for my yoga studio' and the Replit Agent writes the code, sets up a database and puts it online. You do not need to install anything or know how to code. It is free to try, and you pay a monthly plan plus extra for how much work the agent does.

keyNumbers.note: After a $400 million Series D led by Georgian. Tripled from $3 billion in September 2025. AI Magazine and Dealroom.

keyNumbers.note: Company figure via AI Magazine, 2026. Many are old accounts from Replit's coding-for-students era.

keyNumbers.note: CEO Amjad Masad, 2025. Consumer plans likely have much lower margins because of AI model costs.

overview.whatItDoes: Replit is a browser-based tool to build and launch software. Its Agent (Agent 4 since March 2026) takes a plain-language request, writes the code, fixes bugs, creates a database and deploys the app to a live web address. Replit also hosts the app, so users keep paying for it to stay online.
howItWorks: Sign up and describe the app you want in the chat box.
The Agent makes a plan, then writes the code and shows a live preview.
You ask for changes in plain words; the Agent edits and tests again.
Replit sets up a database, logins and payments if needed.
Click Deploy to put the app online on a Replit address or your own domain.
You pay for agent work by 'effort' (bigger tasks cost more) and for hosting.
overview.valueProposition: Go from an idea to a live app in minutes, without hiring a developer or setting anything up.

painPoints.howSolved: The Agent writes the whole app from a plain description.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Builds apps, spreadsheets, data visualisations and games from chat; about 10 times faster than Agent 3.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: This is the core product and the reason Replit's revenue jumped.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Creates a database and user logins automatically.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Real apps need data and logins; doing this for users removes a big blocker.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Puts the app online and keeps it running.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Hosting brings steady monthly revenue after the app is built.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Saves versions so you can undo agent mistakes.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Added after a 2025 incident where an agent deleted a production database; key for trust.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Single sign-on, admin controls and security for company teams.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Enterprise deals have 80 to 90 percent margins.

steps.detail: Watches a YouTube video of someone building an app in 10 minutes.
Types 'Booking app for my yoga studio with UPI payments'.
The Agent lists pages and features; the user approves.
Tries a booking and asks for design changes.
Buys the Core plan to launch on a custom domain.
Links a company database through approved connectors.
Asks the Agent for a sales dashboard.
Adds features based on feedback over a week.
Requests a full redesign and new features.
The Agent runs for many minutes on an effort-based charge.
Monthly credits run out and extra charges appear.
Turns on a spending cap in settings.
Keeps paying or tries Lovable or Bolt instead.

businessModel.summary: Replit makes money from monthly plans, from usage charges for agent work and hosting, and from enterprise seats. The more the Agent builds and the more apps stay online, the more Replit earns. But each agent task also costs Replit money in AI model fees.

revenueStreams.detail: Core and higher plans with monthly usage credits.
Effort-based pricing: bigger, longer agent tasks cost more, billed beyond included credits.
Ongoing fees to keep apps online, plus databases and storage.
About $100 per seat plus usage, with 80 to 90 percent margins.

businessModel.pricing: Starter is free with limited agent use. Core is about $20 to $25 a month with included usage credits. Teams and Enterprise are priced per seat (Enterprise about $100 per seat plus usage). Agent work beyond credits is billed by effort.
costDrivers: AI model fees paid to Anthropic, Google and others for every agent task
Cloud computing for running and hosting apps (Google Cloud is the main provider)
businessModel.unitEconomics: A Core user paying about $25 a month who builds one small app might use $10 to $15 of model costs, leaving some margin. A heavy builder can run up $100s in agent charges in a week, which earns revenue but also costs Replit a lot in model fees. Hosting is high-margin and keeps paying after the app is built. Enterprise seats at $100 plus usage carry 80 to 90 percent margins. Consumer figures are rough estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: Viral demos on X, YouTube and TikTok of apps built in minutes
Millions of existing accounts from Replit's education years
Free tier to try the Agent
Enterprise case studies (Zillow, Rokt, Plaid) and partnerships with Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure and Accenture
Apps built on Replit carry a 'Made with Replit' link
whatBringsUsersBack: Apps live on Replit hosting, so users return to update them
Ongoing changes and new features to their apps
New ideas once the first app works
growth.moat: Replit's moat is that it does everything in one place: code, database, hosting and deploy. Once an app runs on Replit, moving it takes effort. But AI agents are getting easier to build, and rivals like Lovable and Claude Code compete hard.

competitors.name: Lovable
competitors.positioning: Fast-growing European vibe coding tool for web apps.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Lovable is simpler and focused on front-end web apps; Replit covers full apps with databases, hosting and many languages.

competitors.name: Claude Code
competitors.positioning: Anthropic's coding agent, popular with developers.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Claude Code needs some technical setup; Replit is fully in the browser for non-coders. AI Magazine calls Claude Code Replit's biggest competitive problem.

competitors.name: Bolt.new and v0
competitors.positioning: Browser-based AI app builders from StackBlitz and Vercel.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Replit has its own hosting and a larger user base.

competitors.name: Cursor
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Cursor is for programmers; Replit targets people who do not code.

improvementIdeas.idea: Show a price estimate before each agent task and do not charge for failed or reverted attempts
improvementIdeas.problem: Users are shocked by bills and feel charged for agent mistakes.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of users with surprise charges and paid churn

improvementIdeas.idea: Default monthly spending cap at the plan price, which users can raise
improvementIdeas.problem: New users run up big bills without noticing.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer angry complaints and refund requests.

improvementIdeas.idea: Built-in security check before deploy that explains risks in plain words
improvementIdeas.problem: Non-coders cannot see security holes in AI-built apps.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Safer apps and stronger enterprise trust.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Security issues found per deployed app

improvementIdeas.idea: Templates for Indian small businesses with UPI payments, WhatsApp alerts and Hindi pages
improvementIdeas.problem: Small businesses in India need simple apps with local payment methods.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More builders and deployments in a big market.

pmLessons: A pivot to a new customer can save a company. Replit went from about $2.8 million in revenue to a $9 billion valuation by targeting non-coders with agents.
Usage-based pricing matches cost to revenue but can feel unfair. Users need to see and control what they spend.
Owning the full flow (build, host, deploy) creates lock-in and steady revenue.
When AI acts on real data, safety features like checkpoints are part of the product.

interviewQuestions.question: Replit users complain about surprise bills. How would you redesign pricing?
interviewQuestions.hint: Explain why effort-based pricing exists (cost varies). Add estimates, caps and refunds for failures. Track churn and margin together.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the right north star metric for Replit?
interviewQuestions.hint: Apps deployed and still used after 30 days. Break into new builders, deploys, live usage and paying users.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you compete with Lovable?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare target users and strengths. Replit's edge is full-stack and hosting. Pick a segment, like business apps with data, and focus there.

interviewQuestions.question: An agent deleted a user's database. What would you do as PM?
interviewQuestions.hint: Immediate response: restore, apologise, explain. Then prevention: checkpoints, approval for risky actions, separated environments. Measure incidents.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow Replit's enterprise business?
interviewQuestions.hint: Target teams with backlogs of internal tools. Use case studies. Add security and admin controls. Track seats and net revenue retention.
